notes: Boss registry (P2-S6): the REQUIREMENTS §6 bosses, incl. Eater of Worlds / Brain of Cthulhu as world-evil alternatives. Event bosses (Pumpking, Betsy, Celestial Pillars…) are NOT Boss records: AMENDMENTS-001 A3 keeps events as progression markers (overlays/progression.json).

page = the wiki article = the Cargo NPCs/Drops `_page` of the boss rows. npcIds, environment (location.biomes), stats and the sprite file come from Cargo NPCs; this overlay only selects the representative row (`primary`, `sprite`), with `variant` = the row's name note.

statsUnknown: boss-level stats are not one NPC row (multi-part bosses whose parts have their own health or defense) → statsByDifficulty Unknown, reason in the gap report. Other rows go through pipeline/parse/npcStats.ts, which withholds every cell that is not a single integer per difficulty (incl. cells the wiki flags as based on outdated source code).

Every `quote` must occur verbatim on its article (`page` of the entry, or the tag's own `page`); the build checks it against the cached revision. summon.quote is emitted as Boss.summon.text; time is only set when a quote states it (else location.time Unknown).
stage is the editorial five-stage tag (REQUIREMENTS §1); attackPatternTags are editorial (A1 staging: only tags a behavior quote supports; prep/suggested equipment/strategies are P5 overlays).

unlocksStage (AMENDMENTS-005 B22): the stage whose content defeating this boss makes obtainable, set on stage-transition gates only (wall-of-flesh → early-hm: defeating it converts the world to Hardmode). Editorial like stage; validate requires a required-gate edge from the boss to a milestone of exactly that stage (wall-of-flesh → hardmode). Mechanical bosses do not set it: one mech boss does not open mid-hm — the all-mechanical-bosses milestone (mid-hm) does.

summon.quote: King Slime can be summoned by using the Slime Crown, in any biome at any time.

time.quote: in any biome at any time

attackPatternTags.quote: When unable to reach the player, he may teleport to their location.
King Slime attempts to deal contact damage to the player by hopping towards them, and additionally summons slimes to aid him in the fight.
If the player dies or gets more than 187.5 tiles away from King Slime, he will teleport to the bottom-right corner of the world and despawn in 0.17 seconds.
Most bosses and event bosses can pass through blocks of all types, with the exception of King Slime, Queen Slime, Flying Dutchman, and Deerclops (most of the time).

prepChecklist.text: Build one or two long rows of platforms above the ground
prepChecklist.quote: Make one or two long rows of platforms above the ground; King Slime will eventually teleport to ground level and the player can easily hit him from the platforms.

prepChecklist.text: Place Campfires and Heart Lanterns in the arena for health regeneration
prepChecklist.quote: Prepare your Boss-fighting arena with adequate lighting, Campfires and Heart Lanterns for health regeneration, and Stars in Bottles for mana regeneration if you use magic.

prepChecklist.text: Hang a Blue Slime Banner for its offensive and defensive buffs
prepChecklist.quote: Since King Slime spawns Blue Slimes, a Blue Slime Banner is a good idea to provide offensive and defensive buffs.

prepChecklist.text: Bring a long-range weapon to keep a safe distance from his contact damage
prepChecklist.quote: Due to King Slime's high contact damage, using a long-range weapon that can keep a safe distance from him is recommended.

prepChecklist.text: Drink Ironskin and Regeneration Potions
prepChecklist.quote: Ironskin Potions and Regeneration Potions greatly increase survivability.

prepChecklist.text: Drink a Swiftness Potion for mobility
prepChecklist.quote: Swiftness Potions increase mobility.

prepChecklist.text: Equip a double-jump accessory such as a Cloud in a Bottle
prepChecklist.quote: Any double jump accessories such as the Cloud in a Bottle greatly increases vertical mobility.

prepChecklist.text: Carry a stack of the best healing potion you have
prepChecklist.quote: Always carry around a stack of the highest-tier healing potion available, as relying only on natural health regeneration is not a good idea.

strategies.quote: The pattern of his jumps is predictable and repeatedly: two normal, one small, and one high.
After the high jump, the King Slime can teleport to the player.
When King Slime is about to teleport, he shrinks, and his map icon will get closer to the ground.
Getting too far away from King Slime will make it teleport to the player, meaning that the player cannot escape by simply running offscreen.
King Slime becomes smaller and faster the lower his health is, which makes him harder to hit.
Piercing weapons can not only damage King Slime, but also kill the additional slimes he spawns.
If he or his slimes reach the platform, drop down temporarily and use hooks or double-jumps to return; this will cause King Slime and his minions to drop down as well, following you.
King Slime is very slow in liquids.
However, when damaged it will spawn Spiked Slimes in addition to regular Blue Slimes.
strategies.why: The guide's "Expert Mode" section.

strategies.quote: The Thorn Chakram is a good option to keep the boss at range, but can struggle against the hordes of slimes.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Melee users" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: The Ice Blade is a weaker option that is easier to obtain.
strategies.why: Under "For Melee users" (projectile swords paragraph).

strategies.quote: A cheap and powerful option is a bow, such as the Gold, Platinum, or even the Tendon/Demon Bow.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Ranged users" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: Frostburn Arrows or Jester's Arrows are the preferred ammo types, due to the high single target damage of the former and the piercing effect of the latter.
strategies.why: Under "For Ranged users" (bow ammo).

strategies.quote: The Emerald Staff and all stronger staves do well against King Slime.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Magic users" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: The Wand of Frosting is an easily obtained magic weapon that does well in this fight.
strategies.why: Under "For Magic users".

strategies.quote: The best multiple-use summon weapons at this part of the game are the Flinx Staff and the Vampire Frog Staff.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Summoners" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: The Soulscourge and Vasculash are weaker yet easier to obtain alternatives, only requiring mining Demonite or Crimtane.
strategies.why: Under "For Summoners" (whips).

suggestedEquipment.gap: No weapon is verified as obtainable before this fight: the item data does not cover how basic materials, shop stock and chest loot are obtained, and no other boss is a required step before this one. Gear that might not be available is not suggested, so this stays Unknown; the class tips quote the wiki's own gear advice.

summon.quote: The Eye of Cthulhu can be summoned manually using a Suspicious Looking Eye at night (from 7:30 PM to 4:30 AM).

time.quote: using a Suspicious Looking Eye at night

attackPatternTags.quote: The Eye of Cthulhu has two phases and is able to fly through blocks in both of them.
The Eye of Cthulhu has two phases and is able to fly through blocks in both of them.
Afterward, it charges at the player three times in succession, before repeating the cycle.
In the second phase, the Eye of Cthulhu will gain an additional powerful rapid chain dash attack
it attempts to float directly above the player while spawning 3–4 Servants of Cthulhu
If the Eye of Cthulhu is not defeated by dawn (4:30 AM), if all players die, or if it goes too far off-screen, it will despawn.

prepChecklist.text: Build a screen-sized arena with several rows of wooden platforms
prepChecklist.quote: The simplest arena design consists of multiple rows of wooden platforms to have more room to jump and dodge.

prepChecklist.text: Light the arena with Torches: the fight is at night
prepChecklist.quote: As the fight will be at night, add Torches to improve visibility.

prepChecklist.text: Place Campfires and Heart Lanterns in the arena for health regeneration
prepChecklist.quote: Prepare your Boss-fighting arena with adequate lighting, Campfires and Heart Lanterns for health regeneration, and Stars in Bottles for mana regeneration if you use magic.

prepChecklist.text: Summon it just after dusk (7:30 PM) for the most time before dawn
prepChecklist.quote: For nocturnal bosses, starting the battle just after the sun sets (7:30 PM) will provide the maximum amount of time to defeat the boss.

prepChecklist.text: Drink Regeneration, Ironskin and Swiftness Potions
prepChecklist.quote: The most helpful and easily obtainable potions are the Regeneration Potion, the Ironskin Potion, and the Swiftness Potion.

prepChecklist.text: Wear Hermes Boots (or equivalents) to dodge the second phase's rams
prepChecklist.quote: Hermes Boots or equivalents help by making it easier to dodge the second phase's rams.

prepChecklist.text: Bring a Cloud in a Bottle (or equivalent) to avoid the rams
prepChecklist.quote: A Cloud in a Bottle or equivalents can aid in avoiding the rams, although this is less necessary with a good arena.

prepChecklist.text: Carry a stack of the best healing potion you have
prepChecklist.quote: Always carry around a stack of the highest-tier healing potion available, as relying only on natural health regeneration is not a good idea.

strategies.quote: After spawning 3 or 4 Servants, the Eye will charge at you, attempting to ram you 3 times before hovering once more, so be prepared to evade.
It can be helpful to begin to evade after the 3rd servant is spawned, as this will often allow you to dodge its first charge.
The Servants are weak and can be killed for Hearts, or, if there is enough room, the player can simply keep moving in one direction to avoid them.
Make sure to take advantage of its transformation sequence as much as possible, since it just spins in place for a few moments and you can still damage it.
For the last half of the fight, the boss sheds its iris to reveal a fanged mouth. It moves slightly faster and deals more damage when it hits you, but it also has no defense.
With a wide enough arena, running in a straight line while the Eye of Cthulhu does his quick charge is fast enough to avoid any damage, and allows the player to attack continuously.
The boss looks at the player it will follow, which can be helpful information in multiplayer.
In the first phase of the fight it spawns more servants and enters the second phase at 65% health instead of 50%, spawning 4–5 more Servants in that process.
strategies.why: The guide's "Expert and Master Mode" section.

strategies.quote: In this part of the fight, after the 3 normal lunges it will perform a brief series of extremely quick dashes at a steeper angle.
strategies.why: The guide's "Expert and Master Mode" section (second phase).

strategies.quote: Long-range projectile swords can safely attack at a distance.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Melee Users" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: Yoyos have good range and allow for fine control.
strategies.why: Under "For Melee Users".

strategies.quote: Bows are easy to craft and do good damage.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Ranged users" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: Frostburn Arrows deal the most damage to the boss itself and inflict Frostburn, but Jester's Arrows can kill the Servants and hurt the Eye in the same shot.
strategies.why: Under "For Ranged users" (arrows).

strategies.quote: The Wand of Frosting is relatively easy to obtain and inflicts the strong Frostburn debuff.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Magic users" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: The Crimson Rod is an excellent side-weapon, as its clouds can be set up to clear out the servants while also dealing steady damage to the boss.
strategies.why: Under "For Magic users".

strategies.quote: The Cobwhip is the easiest whip to obtain at this point in the game, although it is weaker than other options.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Summoners" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: Two somewhat stronger options are Leather Whip, which can be bought from the Zoologist NPC, and the Slime Whip, which can be crafted at a Solidifier.
strategies.why: Under "For Summoners" (whips).

suggestedEquipment.gap: No weapon is verified as obtainable before this fight: the item data does not cover how basic materials, shop stock and chest loot are obtained, and no other boss is a required step before this one. Gear that might not be available is not suggested, so this stays Unknown; the class tips quote the wiki's own gear advice.

entries.name: Eater of Worlds
entries.statsUnknown: Multi-segment boss: the wiki gives health, defense and damage per segment (head, body and tail rows); no boss-level row.

summon.quote: The Eater of Worlds spawns upon destroying every third Shadow Orb in a Corruption world. It can also be summoned manually by using a Worm Food in The Corruption or Underground Corruption, at any time.

time.quote: in The Corruption or Underground Corruption, at any time

attackPatternTags.quote: While burrowing, it gradually builds up speed in the direction of the player, up to a limit.
If the player dies or is in neither the Corruption nor the Crimson, all of the worms begin fleeing by moving downwards.

prepChecklist.text: Classic Mode: build a tall, thin surface arena that is easy to climb, with many platforms
prepChecklist.quote: In Classic Mode, make it fairly tall, thin, and easily climbable with many platforms.

prepChecklist.text: Keep the arena low enough that the Corruption background stays visible
prepChecklist.quote: If it goes too high and the Corruption background disappears, the Eater of Worlds will start despawning.

prepChecklist.text: If breaking Shadow Orbs, prepare a quick, safe escape to your surface arena
prepChecklist.quote: If summoning this boss via breaking Shadow Orbs, be sure to provide yourself a quick and safe escape back to the surface where your arena will be.

prepChecklist.text: Place a Bed next to the arena so you can teleport there
prepChecklist.quote: A room with a Bed next to your arena can let you teleport there easily, but be careful that the path from the Orb to arena does not go through any non-Corrupted areas (lest the boss despawn).

prepChecklist.text: Hang an Eater of Souls Banner to reduce their damage
prepChecklist.quote: To not get interrupted by the Eaters of Souls, it's recommended to place an Eater of Souls Banner to minimize their damage.

prepChecklist.text: Drink Ironskin and Regeneration Potions
prepChecklist.quote: Ironskin and Regeneration Potions can really help mitigate any hits you take.

prepChecklist.text: Drink a Hunter Potion to spot it while it burrows
prepChecklist.quote: Hunter Potions can be very useful in spotting the Eater of Worlds as it burrows, making it easier to fight even without a raised platform.

prepChecklist.text: Carry a stack of the best healing potion you have
prepChecklist.quote: Always carry around a stack of the highest-tier healing potion available, as relying only on natural health regeneration is not a good idea.

strategies.quote: Beware that, when a segment dies, the segments in front and behind will detach and separately attack the player.
To avoid getting overwhelmed by many worms at once, it may be helpful to only aim for the head or tail of the worm, as these segments will not cause the boss to split further when killed.
If you destroy a middle segment, concentrate on the smaller worm, since the larger one can be easy to predict and dodge.

Like other worm enemies, once the Eater's head passes a given point, every body segment must follow. This allows the player to stand next to the body, attacking every segment as it goes by. The player should be wary of the head looping back around.
In Classic Mode, Grenades are an effective weapon against the Eater. That is not true in higher difficulties, since the Eater gains resistance to explosives.
The Eater of Worlds will start to flee underground if the player leaves the Corruption biome, but will not immediately despawn.
Vile Spit is the Eater of Worlds' most dangerous attack, so it is important to bring sufficient mobility accessories and make an arena that enables you to dodge.
strategies.why: The guide's "Expert Mode" section (Vile Spit is an Expert Mode attack).

strategies.quote: Broadswords do very well against this boss.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Melee users" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: Spears such as the Swordfish can damage multiple segments at once, and are most effective if you try to line them up with the boss's length.
strategies.why: Under "For Melee users".

strategies.quote: Jester's Arrows can pierce through infinitely many segments, although the damage drops each segment.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Ranged users" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: The Demon Bow is easily available and powerful.
strategies.why: Under "For Ranged users" (bows).

strategies.quote: The Vilethorn is good for spreading damage across the boss's entire body.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Magic users" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: Topaz's small explosion is very helpful in this fight, shredding through segments of the boss.
strategies.why: Under "For Magic users" (gem staves and robes).

strategies.quote: The Flinx Staff is consistently available and can damage a lot of segments at once if spread out.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Summoners" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: Pairing 1 Vampire Frog and 2 Flinx will grant the most DPS available for summoners.
strategies.why: Under "For Summoners".

suggestedEquipment.gap: No weapon is verified as obtainable before this fight: the item data does not cover how basic materials, shop stock and chest loot are obtained, and no other boss is a required step before this one. Gear that might not be available is not suggested, so this stays Unknown; the class tips quote the wiki's own gear advice.

summon.quote: The Brain of Cthulhu spawns upon destroying every third Crimson Heart in a Crimson world. It can also be summoned manually by using a Bloody Spine in The Crimson or Underground Crimson, at any time.

time.quote: in The Crimson or Underground Crimson, at any time

attackPatternTags.quote: In the first, the Brain is immune to damage and teleports randomly around the player.
Twenty Creepers spawn along with the Brain and orbit the boss at high speed.
The Brain of Cthulhu's battle is composed of two phases.
both the Creepers (in the first phase) and the Brain (in the second phase) inflict a random debuff upon contact.
If the player leaves the Crimson, the Brain of Cthulhu will move downwards and despawn.

prepChecklist.text: Set up rows of platforms across the Chasm's central chamber and light it up
prepChecklist.quote: Set up several rows of platforms all the way across the central chamber, close enough that you can jump up to the next platform, and light up everything.

prepChecklist.text: Block off the entrances of nearby chambers so enemies can't enter
prepChecklist.quote: Block off entrances to the small chambers nearby with blocks so enemies can't enter your arena.

prepChecklist.text: Place Peace Candles or drink a Calming Potion before the fight
prepChecklist.quote: Alternatively, place Peace Candles in your arena or drink a Calming Potion before starting the fight.

prepChecklist.text: Using a Bloody Spine: keep a surface arena low so you stay in the Crimson
prepChecklist.quote: If summoned with the Bloody Spine, then the arena can simply be made in the surface, however, do not make it very tall, as jumping too far above it will be considered exiting The Crimson, causing the Brain of Cthulhu to despawn.

prepChecklist.text: Drink Ironskin, Swiftness and Regeneration Potions
prepChecklist.quote: The Ironskin Potion, the Swiftness Potion and the Regeneration Potion will increase survivability.

prepChecklist.text: Equip a Cloud in a Bottle for a double jump
prepChecklist.quote: The Cloud in a Bottle will give you a double-jump ability which will greatly help with evasion.

prepChecklist.text: Wear Hermes Boots for speed
prepChecklist.quote: The Hermes Boots will increase your speed and aid greatly in evasion.

prepChecklist.text: Carry a stack of the best healing potion you have
prepChecklist.quote: Always carry around a stack of the highest-tier healing potion available, as relying only on natural health regeneration is not a good idea.

strategies.quote: Brain of Cthulhu has 2 phases, with the latter starting after all Creepers have been dealt with.
Jump out of the way, either by using your platforms or with an extra jump, then attack the Creepers. Use piercing weapons to speed up the process.
Creepers have low individual health and are especially susceptible to the On Fire! and Frostburn debuffs.

When all of the Creepers are dead, the Brain will split, revealing a Heart with an Eye on the inside. The Brain teleports much more frequently, often at unexpected angles, and will try to ram into you.
If you have a weapon with high knockback, it will excel at dealing with the Brain, so much so that it's possible to stand in one location and attack it whenever it gets close.
During the second phase, the Brain will spawn clones of itself around the player.
strategies.why: The guide's "Expert Mode" section.

strategies.quote: Life-draining debuffs such as On Fire! and Frostburn will help distinguish them. Additionally, summoned minions and sentries will always target the correct copy.
strategies.why: The guide's "Expert Mode" section (telling the clones apart).

strategies.quote: The real Brain is the only one with a health bar.
strategies.why: From the article's list of ways to reveal the real Brain among its illusions; the guide's "Expert Mode" section is where the clones appear.

strategies.quote: A spear is a good weapon against the Brain of Cthulhu during the second stage.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Melee users:" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: A flail of some kind is beneficial for taking out the Creepers; the easiest to obtain would be the Flaming Mace (craftable from a Mace, which can be found in Gold Chests located underground).
strategies.why: Under "For Melee users:".

strategies.quote: Tendon Bow is an easily obtainable and powerful bow at this stage.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Ranged users:" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: You can combine them with either Unholy Arrows or Jester's Arrows, which greatly help to kill the swarm of Creepers.
strategies.why: Under "For Ranged users:" (arrows for the bows).

strategies.quote: The Crimson Rod is a great support weapon that can easily be obtained through Crimson Hearts.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Magic users:" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: A Diamond Staff is very good at taking out the Creepers because of its high fire rate, large hitbox and pierce.
strategies.why: Under "For Magic users:".

strategies.quote: If the Snapthorn is too difficult to obtain, one can use the Vasculash, which is a weaker alternative.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Summoners:" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: The summon tag icon will linger on the correct Brain, which may be helpful in identifying the correct copy.
strategies.why: Under "For Summoners:" (whip tag marks the real Brain).

Gear that might not be available is not suggested, so this stays Unknown; the class tips quote the wiki's own gear advice.

summon.quote: The Queen Bee spawns upon breaking a Larva found inside Bee Hives in the Underground Jungle. She can also be summoned manually by using an Abeemination in the Jungle or Underground Jungle, at any time.

time.quote: in the Jungle or Underground Jungle, at any time

attackPatternTags.quote: The Queen Bee levels herself horizontally with the player before charging back and forth three times in an attempt to ram the player.
The Queen Bee spawns Bees while hovering (which includes larger ones in Expert Mode), which pursue and attack the player.
The Queen Bee rapidly fires large yellow stingers at the player
she will inflict the Poisoned debuff upon direct contact with the player
When fought outside of the Underground Jungle, the Queen Bee enrages

prepChecklist.text: Fight in a Hive: it is already carved out and its honey pool regenerates health
prepChecklist.quote: However, most Hives offer an easy arena: a decent amount of space is already carved out, and the pool of honey at the bottom provides a health-regenerating buff which stacks with other buffs.

prepChecklist.text: Stay in the Underground Jungle: outside it she enrages
prepChecklist.quote: When fought outside of the Underground Jungle, the Queen Bee enrages

prepChecklist.text: Place Wood Platforms about every 5 blocks
prepChecklist.quote: Having them every 5 blocks is an optimal height but if the player's jump height is boosted in some way, the number of spaces between platforms can be increased which can save materials.

prepChecklist.text: Clear Larvae near the arena so you don't summon a second Queen Bee
prepChecklist.quote: Make sure that there are no Larvae within the vicinity of the arena, as to not accidentally break a Larva, summoning another Queen Bee.

prepChecklist.text: Equip a Bezoar to remove the Poisoned debuff
prepChecklist.quote: The Bezoar, while equipped, removes the Poisoned debuff; to save on accessory slots, equip it whenever the character is poisoned.

prepChecklist.text: Drink Ironskin, Endurance and Regeneration Potions
prepChecklist.quote: Ironskin Potions, Endurance Potions, and Regeneration Potions will help tremendously with survivability.

prepChecklist.text: Drink a Swiftness Potion to help dodge
prepChecklist.quote: Swiftness Potions will aid in dodging.

prepChecklist.text: Craft Bottled Honey from the Hive's honey
prepChecklist.quote: The Honey naturally found in Bee Hives can be used to craft Bottled Honey, provide passive health regeneration mid-fight, and help to negate the potency of being afflicted by Poisoned.

strategies.quote: When she charges you, use platforms and/or a double jump or better to dodge upwards.
When she summons her Bees, use a weapon that can pierce targets and aim for her tail to stop the Bees the moment they spawn.
If any Bees manage to escape then use a sword with a large swing to clear them out.
If she's using the stinger-shooting phase, keep moving back and forth.
Getting hit by a stinger inflicts a Poisoned debuff that will last longer than running into Queen Bee, so make sure to dodge it.
Solid blocks can help to block the stingers.
Queen Bee is one of the few bosses that does not despawn when the player teleports away.
As the Queen Bee's health goes down, she will become a lot more aggressive, shooting more stingers and having much faster charges.
strategies.why: The guide's "Expert Mode" section.

strategies.quote: Successfully dashing into an enemy gives the player brief invincibility frames, so if timed right, the charge attacks can be completely neutralized.
strategies.why: The guide's "Expert Mode" section (the dash of the Expert-only Shield of Cthulhu).

strategies.quote: Swords can be surprisingly effective, doing the most damage when the Queen Bee is releasing Bees or when charging you.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Melee users" weapons heading.

strategies.quote: The Thorn Chakram, Trimarang, or Flamarang are good at killing the Queen Bee, due to their long range.
strategies.why: Under "For Melee users".

strategies.quote: Bring along arrows that can pierce, such as Jester's Arrows or Unholy Arrows.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Ranged users" weapons heading (bows).

strategies.quote: Note that the Minishark is much less effective in Expert Mode, especially in the latter stages of the battle, unless paired with the Shark Tooth Necklace.
strategies.why: Under "For Ranged users"; the sentence is about Expert Mode.

strategies.quote: Amethyst's homing ability is very helpful in this fight, being able to track the boss when she's dashing.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Magic users" weapons heading (gem staves and robes).

strategies.quote: The Space Gun is a good weapon, especially when combined with Meteor armor. Its piercing effect will help with taking out the Bees.
strategies.why: Under "For Magic users".

strategies.quote: Summoners should use the Flinx Staff or, preferably, the Vampire Frog Staff, together with one of the early whips.
strategies.why: Under the guide's "For Summoners" weapons heading.

suggestedEquipment.gap: No weapon is verified as obtainable before this fight: the item data does not cover how basic materials, shop stock and chest loot are obtained, and no other boss is a required step before this one. Gear that might not be available is not suggested, so this stays Unknown; the class tips quote the wiki's own gear advice.

summon.quote: Summoning Skeletron requires the player to speak to the Old Man at the Dungeon's entrance at night. Upon selecting the "Curse" option, he will turn into Skeletron. Skeletron can only be summoned once per night, as the Old Man will not respawn until dawn. Once Skeletron is defeated, the Old Man's curse will be lifted and he will no longer appear. Skeletron will thereafter only be summonable with the Clothier Voodoo Doll. Killing the Clothier at night with this accessory equipped will summon Skeletron.

time.quote: speak to the Old Man at the Dungeon's entrance at night

attackPatternTags.quote: the head begins to shoot homing skulls at the player
Skeletron will inflict debuffs upon contact with the player
If the player takes too long to kill Skeletron and dawn (4:30 AM) arrives, it will enrage

prepChecklist.text: Plan the arena above the Dungeon roof or beside the Dungeon
prepChecklist.quote: It is generally more convenient to plan the arena above the Dungeon roof or to the side of the Dungeon.

prepChecklist.text: Leave the Dungeon floor intact: edits there can stop the Cultists spawning later
prepChecklist.quote: Don't make significant edits to the Dungeon floor. Doing so can stop the Endgame Cultists from spawning, potentially blocking progression.

prepChecklist.text: Leave room to dodge the hands and vertical space for the head spin
prepChecklist.quote: Most important is that there is enough room to dodge the hands, as well as enough vertical space to avoid getting trapped when Skeletron's head begins to spin.

prepChecklist.text: Start early in the night: it enrages if not defeated by 4:30 AM
prepChecklist.quote: Failing to defeat it before 4:30 AM in-game will cause Skeletron to enrage.

prepChecklist.text: Drink Ironskin, Endurance and Regeneration Potions
prepChecklist.quote: Ironskin Potions, Endurance Potions, and Regeneration Potions will make the job easier for any player and are highly recommended.

prepChecklist.text: Drink a Swiftness Potion to outrun the spinning attack
prepChecklist.quote: The Swiftness Potion helps for outrunning the spinning attack.

prepChecklist.text: Drink a Featherfall Potion for air mobility
prepChecklist.quote: Featherfall Potions can aid with air mobility and give basic flying abilities.

prepChecklist.text: Bring a grappling hook to escape the head-spin attack
prepChecklist.quote: Using a grappling hook can also help evade Skeletron's attacks and is an especially useful tool to escape its head-spin attack.

strategies.quote: Attacking the hands first is advised, as destroying them both will make it very easy to dodge Skeletron for the rest of the battle. This is pretty much mandatory in Expert Mode, as Skeletron gains 25 defense for each hand it has alive.
Timing is key in order to defend from the hands: after dodging them, use piercing weapons to deal damage to both arms (and Skeletron's skull, if it happens to align with them).
Try to avoid staying above or far to one side of Skeletron for a long time.

After some time, Skeletron will use its spinning attack. Skeletron moves slowly, but they constantly follow the player. During this attack, Skeletron's defense is lowered to zero, but gains more attack. The player should use the fastest weapon at their disposal to deal a lot of damage. However, make sure to constantly move; if the player gets hit by it, they might get stunlocked and take a lot of damage.
Skulls are blocked by solid blocks, so a barrier between the player and Skeletron can let the player attack Skeletron using a yoyo with impunity.
In Expert Mode, if the player keeps moving in different directions, most of the homing skulls will miss.
strategies.why: The sentence is about Expert Mode.

prepChecklist.text: Clear a large flat area in the Snow biome
prepChecklist.quote: It is recommended to clear a large flat area in the Snow biome.

prepChecklist.text: Set your spawn point away from where Deerclops can wander
prepChecklist.quote: Players should place their spawn point away from where Deerclops can wander, as it can stay around the spawn area.

prepChecklist.text: Drink a Warmth Potion: its buff cuts Deerclops's damage by 30%
prepChecklist.quote: Warmth Potions will reduce Deerclop's damage by 30% and reduce the duration of the inflicted Frozen and Chilled debuffs, using one will greatly increase survivability.

prepChecklist.text: Equip a Hand Warmer against the Frozen debuff
prepChecklist.quote: In addition, one may find it useful to bring a Hand Warmer to the battle, since the Frozen debuff can easily cause the player to die quickly if inflicted.

prepChecklist.text: Drink Ironskin, Endurance and Regeneration Potions
prepChecklist.quote: Ironskin Potions, Endurance Potions, Warmth Potions, and Regeneration Potions will help tremendously with survivability.

prepChecklist.text: Drink a Swiftness Potion to help dodge
prepChecklist.quote: Swiftness Potions will aid in dodging.

prepChecklist.text: Equip a Cloud in a Bottle (or a better jump accessory)
prepChecklist.quote: The Cloud in a Bottle is good, but better choices would be the Blizzard in a Bottle, Fart in a Jar, or Sandstorm in a Bottle and its upgrades, especially the Bundle of Balloons.

prepChecklist.text: Carry a stack of the best healing potion you have
prepChecklist.quote: Always carry around a stack of the highest-tier healing potion available, as relying only on natural health regeneration is not a good idea.

strategies.quote: Avoid lingering directly above Deerclops, as the Shadow Hands it summons in this situation are very dangerous.
The player can run between Deerclops's legs without taking damage. This is useful for avoiding the first two Ice Spike attacks, but the player should not stick around for the third.

If it is close to the player, Deerclops will smash the ground, summoning a wave of Ice Spikes that quickly travels towards the player. Every third consecutive wave does not go as far, instead spreading in both directions.

If the player is more than 30 tiles away, Deerclops will turn a dark shade of purple, two reddish, semi-transparent images of Deerclops will begin spinning around it, and it becomes immune to all damage.
Due to being able to inflict Slow from a large range, accessories like the Anklet of the Wind or Magiluminescence alongside Swiftness Potions can help make the fight much more manageable.
The Frozen debuff from the Ice Spike attack is capable of interrupting a player's extending grappling hook, causing them to drop to the ground.
Shadow Hands are summoned more frequently as Deerclops's life gets lower. Shadow Hands predict the player's movements.
strategies.why: The guide's "Expert Mode" section (the fifth attack).
